The main takeaway from our work is that
bone involvement is a frequent feature of monogenic AID syndromes, which should prompt clinicians to consider these conditions in the differential diagnosis of children with unexplained bone lesions.

AIDs are not only a group of rare diseases but a paradigm of how genetic and clinical heterogeneity can be used to identify new pathophysiological mechanisms, which in turn can be translated to the treatment of other more common diseases.
